source_name: Direktorat za politiku javnih nabavki (former Uprava za javne nabavke) — ujn.gov.me
source_subtype: regulator / policy directorate + annual statistical report
why_relevant: Policy owner and publisher of the annual Izvještaj o javnim nabavkama, which aggregates concluded-contract values, procedure types and direct-award shares (2025 report: ~EUR 990m contracted, 12.44% of GDP). Also hosts standard forms, the consolidated procurement law, monitoring manuals and an EU-tenders category — the best pointer for identifying which registers and obligations exist and where they publish.

source_name: Državna revizorska institucija Crne Gore (DRI) — audit reports + own procurement section
source_subtype: supreme audit institution reports + per-authority contract page
why_relevant: Two distinct values. (a) DRI audit reports on individual state bodies (e.g. Uprava prihoda i carina, Agencija za investicije) itemise concluded contracts, values and procurement irregularities — a rich retrospective record of who supplied what to whom. (b) DRI's own /javne-nabavke page publishes its procurement plans and concluded contracts, i.e. a working example of the per-authority publication obligation that cell #2 must cover across all contracting authorities.

source_name: Skupština Crne Gore — Plan javne nabavke
why_relevant: Concrete template of the per-authority annual-plan publication duty: a dedicated 'Plan javne nabavke' page under a public-facing 'javne nabavke' section. Establishes the URL/menu convention (/javne-nabavke/plan-javne-nabavke) that can be probed across other Montenegrin authorities' sites, which is how the forward-looking January pipeline signal is harvested at scale.

source_name: Komunalne usluge Podgorica — Javne nabavke (municipal utility, per-authority pattern)
why_relevant: Second independent instance of the per-authority '/javne-nabavke/' publication convention, this time at municipal/utility level. Utilities are heavy buyers of billing, cash-collection and payment-acceptance systems, so their plan and contract pages are a genuine payments-adjacent outcome channel distinct from central government.

source_name: Institut alternativa — public procurement analysis stream
why_relevant: Think tank that publishes running commentary on the government's annual procurement report, on the growth of direct awards, and on urgent/shortened procedures of multi-million value. It also proposes what the annual report should disclose (contract amendments, unauthorised direct agreements, non-reporting contractors) — which doubles as a map of the metadata gaps in the official outcome record.

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily, Montenegro contract award notices
source_subtype: supranational award-notice register with API/bulk data
why_relevant: Publishes contract award notices for Montenegro-located procurements, typically EU/IPA-financed ones, in structured form with the winning supplier and awarded value (a Montenegro-Podgorica award of EUR 2,144,491.25 to a Podgorica supplier appears as an example). This is a machine-readable outcome channel that does not depend on scraping CEJN, and it captures donor-funded modernisation projects that often carry the payments/IT content.

source_name: UJN 'EU tenderi' category — Montenegrin republication of EU-financed notices
why_relevant: Bridges the national and EU channels: the Directorate republishes EU-financed tender and award items locally, which lets EU-funded contract outcomes be caught in a single national feed and cross-linked back to TED records.

source_name: gov.me / wapi.gov.me document store — government-hosted procurement PDFs
why_relevant: Central government portal publishes individual award decisions as articles ('Odluka o izboru najpovoljnije ponude po Javnom oglasu za dostavljanje ponuda') and serves the underlying documents from wapi.gov.me/download/{uuid}. Annual work reports of the procurement-appeals commission and World Bank/Government procurement assessments are hosted the same way. This is the catch-all channel for ministries and agencies that publish outside CEJN's UI.

source_name: Monstat (Zavod za statistiku) — javne nabavke / ugovori document folder
why_relevant: A working example of an authority that dumps its award decisions and contracts into a directly fetchable static folder (path literally .../javne nabavke/ugovori/...), bypassing any portal. Confirms that per-authority static document trees are a viable, low-friction harvesting route, and gives a template path to probe on other .org/.me authority sites.

source_name: Investitor.me — business press coverage of procurement totals and awards
why_relevant: Montenegrin business media that reports on the annual procurement aggregate (e.g. 'Javne nabavke u Crnoj Gori dostigle skoro milijardu eura', May 2026) and on individual notable awards. Press is the earliest human-readable signal that a large contract has been signed, often days before the formal record is easy to find, and it names suppliers.

source_name: Bankar.me — banking/finance trade press for Montenegro
why_relevant: Sector-specific outlet covering Montenegrin banks, IRF/Razvojna banka and payment topics. Relevant to the outcome side because private-sector banks are not covered by the public-procurement registers at all: for those buyers, a vendor selection only becomes visible through trade press, bank press releases and supplier announcements.

source_name: Erste Bank Montenegro — saopštenja (bank public notices as private-sector outcome proxy)
source_subtype: private-sector issuer notices (pattern applies across all ME banks)
why_relevant: Commercial banks publish saopštenja announcing card-scheme launches, fee decisions and new payment products (e.g. a MasterCard Debit announcement with an accompanying Odluka o naknadama). These are the closest available proxy for a private-sector 'award': they reveal which scheme, processor or technology a bank has actually adopted and roughly when it went live, since no contract register covers private banks.

source_name: eu.me — Montenegro EU-integration portal, procurement alignment reporting
why_relevant: Official EU-integration communication describing CEJN's scope in authoritative terms — that all public calls, plans, decisions, complaints and contract implementation must be available through CEJN, with user counts. Best single citation for what the outcome-side register is legally supposed to contain, and a pointer to Chapter 5 (public procurement) accession documentation.

source_name: CBCG – Registar banaka (Register of banks)
why_relevant: Authoritative enumeration of every licensed bank in Montenegro. Each bank is a buyer of POS/ATM/card-personalisation/software and most run their own tender or 'javni poziv' pages; this register defines the buyer population that other A2 cells must then mine individually.

source_name: CBCG – Registri (payment-system registers hub page)
why_relevant: Hub page confirmed to link four separate registers (payment systems, payment institutions + agents, e-money institutions + agents, revoked authorisations). Single best snowball entry point for the licensed-payments actor population in ME.

source_name: CBCG – Registar platnih institucija i njihovih agenata
why_relevant: Full list of licensed payment institutions and their agents — the non-bank acquirer/PSP layer that buys terminals, gateways and fiscalisation-compliant POS software. Names here become the seed set for company-level tender and contract-award searches.

source_name: CBCG – Registar institucija za elektronski novac i njihovih agenata
why_relevant: E-money institution register: identifies fintech/EMI actors likely to procure card issuing, KYC, tokenisation and terminal services. Small population, high signal for a payments-vendor market map.

source_name: CBCG – Spisak platnih institucija i institucija za elektronski novac kojima je oduzeto odobrenje
why_relevant: Negative-list companion register (revoked authorisations). Prevents chasing dead actors and flags market exits — useful for dating changes in the buyer population between snapshots.

source_name: CBCG – Registar platnih sistema
why_relevant: Enumerates the licensed payment systems/operators in ME. Payment-system operators are direct buyers of switching, clearing and settlement infrastructure — a small but high-value tender-issuing population.

source_name: CBCG – Centralni registar transakcionih računa pravnih lica i preduzetnika
why_relevant: Central register of legal-entity transaction accounts: maps which company banks with which bank. Reveals-indirectly the bank–corporate relationship graph and confirms a legal entity's existence/identifiers for entity resolution against tender award notices.

source_name: CBCG – Pretraga blokiranih pravnih lica i preduzetnika (blocked-accounts search)
why_relevant: Blocked-account / enforced-collection search. Financial-distress screen on bidders and awardees appearing in procurement records; also a due-diligence pointer when assessing local partners or competitors.

source_name: CRPS – Centralni registar privrednih subjekata (public search)
why_relevant: The master company register of Montenegro (legal form, status, founding date, legal representatives). This is the backbone for resolving bidder/awardee names found in tender notices into real legal entities, and for enumerating vendors by activity code.

source_name: eFirma / CRPS portal (Uprava prihoda i carina)
why_relevant: The tax-administration-hosted face of CRPS, used for e-registration of companies and for accessing company records including beneficial ownership. Alternative access path if pretraga.crps.me is unstable; also documents the registration obligation for foreign software vendors selling into ME.
